title: Local Linear Attention: An Optimal Interpolation of Linear and Softmax Attention For Test-Time Regression
claim: Global linear fits are too rigid and local averaging is biased at boundaries; combining locality with linear fitting gives the best bias-variance trade-off.
layout: 3 sections left-to-right: fit plot, theory flow, stacked method panels with kernel+fit icons
description: The figure has three parts. On the left is a scatter plot of noisy blue points around a gray sinusoidal ground-truth curve. Position runs along the x-axis from 0 to 1024, with dashed vertical lines marking segment boundaries. Within each segment, a green line (Mesa) is a single global linear fit. A red curve (Attn) is a local average that drifts at segment edges. A blue curve (LLA) follows the truth closely, including at the boundaries. A legend sits below the plot. In the middle, serif text is linked by arrows: Bias-Variance Trade-off, Mean Square Error, and Associative Memory Distortion. Under it is a row of key (k), value (v), and query (q) tokens. On the right, three tinted panels are stacked vertically: Linear Attention Family (green), Softmax Attention (red), and Local Linear Attention (blue). Each pairs a kernel-weight icon with a scatter plot and a fitted line or star-shaped averaging lines. The eye goes first to the colored curves on the left, then to the right-hand panels.
caption: A comparison of regression strategies: global linear models (e.g., SSMs, MesaNet, DeltaNet) employ query agnostic linear fits and suffer from irreducible approximation error due to model misspecification; local constant models (e.g., Softmax Attention) perform query-specific local averaging but exhibit boundary bias; local linear models (e.g., LLA) achieve a superior bias-variance trade-off combining locality and linear fitting.
abstract: Transformer architectures have achieved remarkable success in various domains. While efficient alternatives to Softmax Attention have been widely studied, the search for more expressive mechanisms grounded in theoretical insight-even at greater computational cost-has been relatively underexplored. In this work, we bridge this gap by proposing Local Linear Attention (LLA), a novel attention mechanism derived from nonparametric statistics through the lens of test-time regression. First, we show that LLA offers theoretical advantages over Linear and Softmax Attention for associative memory via a bias-variance trade-off analysis. Next, we address its computational challenges and propose two memory-efficient primitives to tackle the $Î(n^2 d)$ and $Î(n d^2)$ complexity. We then introduce FlashLLA, a hardware-efficient, blockwise algorithm that enables scalable and parallel computation on modern accelerators. In addition, we implement and profile a customized inference kernel that significantly reduces memory overheads. Finally, we empirically validate the advantages and limitations of LLA on test-time regression, in-context regression, associative recall and state tracking tasks. Experiment results demonstrate that LLA effectively adapts to non-stationarity, outperforming strong baselines in test-time training and in-context learning, and exhibiting promising evidence for its scalability and applicability in large-scale models. Code is available at https://github.com/Yifei-Zuo/Flash-LLA.
